discovery: Electromagnetic metamaterials and transformation optics: negative refraction, the perfect lens and invisibility cloaking
subfield: Optics and photonics / electromagnetic wave physics
motivation: Pendry showed that structuring matter below the wavelength creates electromagnetic properties absent in nature: artificial magnetism, negative permittivity and permeability, and a 'perfect lens' that beats the diffraction limit (2000). Smith realised the first negative-index metamaterial and demonstrated negative refraction (2000-2001), turning Veselago's curiosity into a laboratory fact. In 2006 Pendry and, independently, Leonhardt introduced transformation optics: Maxwell's equations are form-invariant under coordinate transformations, so a medium can mimic curved space and steer light at will. Smith's team then built the first microwave invisibility cloak. These ideas founded a new field with reach far beyond optics: acoustic, thermal, seismic and elastic metamaterials, analogue gravity, metasurfaces and flat optics now in commercial products. This is conceptual originality of the highest order, combining a universal wave principle with transformative technology.
